lede: **Nothing here is placed by name** — no unlock beacon, no wormhole — so what you get is decided entirely by the order the lines are filled. The stores and the distress beacons land before a single fight is placed and are effectively certain; the deep neutral pool at the bottom, the one carrying the **Damaged Stasis Pod**, is where a full map runs out of room. Rock space is generous at the top of the table and thin at the bottom.
callout: **Versus the Rock Homeworlds:** the same eight entries in the same order, the same pools, the same numbers. The homeworlds bolt two named beacons on top — the Rock Cruiser test and the Crystal wormhole — and because those sit above everything else in the definition, they are the two things that sector can never fail to place. This one repeats and names nothing; the homeworlds arrive at most once a run and no earlier than sector 5.

section_notes.STORE_ROCK: First in the queue, so this is the one line nothing can squeeze out: whatever else the sector fails to place, the resupply happens. Three other events can open a shop on top of it — {{ESCORT_BEACON}} from the distress line, {{QUEST_ESCORT}} and {{MERCENARY_WORK_START}} from the 0–1 quest line near the bottom.
section_notes.DISTRESS_BEACON_ROCK: Filled third, before a single fight is placed, so these beacons are as reliable as the stores — and they are the best line in the sector: twelve events, ten of them carrying a blue option, four of the five that can kill a crew member outright. Two of the twelve, {{PIRATE_CIVILIAN_BEACON}} and {{REBEL_VS_FEDERATION}}, carry no distress tag, so a slot from this line does not always put a marker on the map.
section_notes.HOSTILE_ROCK: Five events, every one of them a Rock ship, and three arrive with the environment already against you — twice in an asteroid field, once beside a sun. Each is combat at the root: the beacon opens with weapons live. This line is filled fourth, so the fights are as certain as the stores.
section_notes.BOARDERS_ROCK: {{ROCK_BOARDERS_SUN}} is the odd one — no ship fight and no choice at all, two to three Rockmen aboard the instant you arrive with the sun on your hull the whole time. The other two pair a ship with the teleport, one of them inside an asteroid field.
section_notes.ITEMS: Thirteen events of free kit, traders and stations, and none of them are marked on the map — unlike a store or a distress call, you cannot route towards one. {{HELP_MINERS}} is the one that pays an augment, and it wants missiles for it.
section_notes.QUESTS_ROCK: Zero is a legal roll **and** this line is second-to-last, so it is the least reliable thing on the table twice over. The distress line above it plants markers regardless — {{CIVILIAN_ASTEROIDS_BEACON}}, {{REBEL_VS_FEDERATION}} and {{ESCORT_BEACON}} all start quests — while {{ROCK_QUEST_MARRIAGE_START}} is the only starter that is Rock's own.
section_notes.NEUTRAL_ROCK: Ten events, the deepest pool in the sector, and the last line filled — everything above it can claim up to twenty of the map's twenty-four beacons, so this is where a full map runs out. It is also the only line carrying a named item: {{ASTEROID_DERELICT_SHIP}} is the **Damaged Stasis Pod**, and Rock Plating collapses its three-way search into the single branch that finds it. The start of the Crystal route is therefore the first thing this sector will drop.

steps.title: {{ROCK_QUEST_MARRIAGE_START}}
steps.detail: A stranded Rock captain asks you to carry his passenger to her arranged husband. **Accept the passenger** plants the marker; refusing ends it on the spot. She will not enter the main hold and waits in the cargo bay.

steps.title: Numa V
steps.detail: The tunnel network of an advanced Rock civilisation. On arrival the passenger — silent the whole trip — begs you not to hand her over, and the Grand Basilisk's Chief Aid opens the channel to demand delivery.

steps.title: Two ways to end it
steps.detail: Hand her over and the guards drop off an exotic augment and a little scrap. Refuse and she joins you as **Ariadne**, a Rock crew member — then the Basilisk's escort opens fire and you fight a Rock warship on the way out.

items.text: The widest gate in the sector. Level 2 turns the plain appeal at {{ROCK_ATHIEST}} into a certain Rock crew member, and opens branches at {{CIVILIAN_ASTEROIDS_BEACON}}, {{REBEL_VS_FEDERATION}}, {{FEDERATION_PLANET_SIGNAL}} and {{TRADER_UPGRADES}}.

{{ROCK_MANTIS_HUNTER}}, {{DISTRESS_STATION_FIRE}} and {{DISTRESS_STATION_DISEASE}}. A Rockman walks straight into the burning station and the scientists pay an augment for it; on the mining colony the immunity alone is worth a reward. Rockmen are also the crew most likely to be on the shelf in this sector's stores.
Ram the hunter at {{ROCK_MANTIS_HUNTER}} and its engines are dead before the shooting starts; guarantee the pod at {{ASTEROID_DERELICT_SHIP}}; and a third opening at {{CIVILIAN_ASTEROIDS_BEACON}}.
{{FRIENDLY_SLAVER}}, {{CIVILIAN_ASTEROIDS_BEACON}}, {{REBEL_VS_FEDERATION}} and {{QUEST_CREWDEAD_START}}, where it is one of only three keys in, alongside an Anti-Bio Beam and a Fire Bomb.
{{ROCK_MANTIS_FREIGHTER}}, {{CIVILIAN_ASTEROIDS_BEACON}}, and sending the drone into the flames at {{DISTRESS_STATION_FIRE}} for a drone schematic instead of a coin flip with a crew member's life.
A lookout while you strip the wreck at {{ROCK_LOOTING}} — both of its outcomes pay and neither ends in a fight — and a read on what is really down there at {{STRANDED_BEACON}}.
**Damaged Stasis Pod** at {{ASTEROID_DERELICT_SHIP}} — the only named item the whole pool hands out, and it sits in the one line the map can starve.
Rockmen two ways: talked round at {{ROCK_ATHIEST}}, where Improved Sensors makes it certain and the plain appeal is one outcome in three, or bought at {{FRIENDLY_SLAVER}}.

{{FRIENDLY_SLAVER}} is the one beacon that can produce a Mantis, a Rockman or an Engi; {{TAVERN_HIRE}} sells outright; {{STRANDED_BEACON}} can hand you a human off a moon with a level already in something.
26 of the 50 events in the pool can add someone — over half the sector, against five that can take someone away.
A free reactor bar is one of three follow-ups at {{ROCK_SLUG_ARGUMENT}} if you settle the Rock ship's debt for 10–15 scrap; another of the three sells you the same upgrade at the same price.
A high-tier weapon out of {{DISTRESS_STATION_DISEASE}} — but only with an upgraded Medbay **and** the Engi Med-bot Dispersal to spread the cure.

Five events can kill a crew member outright, four of them inside the distress line: {{DISTRESS_INFESTATION}}, {{DISTRESS_STATION_FIRE}}, {{DISTRESS_STATION_DISEASE}} and {{STRANDED_BEACON}}. The fifth is {{ROCK_STARSHIP_MINE}}. That line is filled early, so the risk arrives early too.

Five of the eight hostile and boarding events open inside a hazard — three asteroid fields, two suns — and a hazard freezes the ship menu while you sit in it: no upgrades, no cargo swaps, no crew reassignment until you jump. At the suns, holding shields up keeps a flare to one or two fires instead of three to six.
Four events put someone aboard. Three are Rockmen, up to three of them at {{ROCK_BOARDERS_SHIP}} and at {{ROCK_BOARDERS_SUN}}; {{FEDERATION_PLANET_SIGNAL}} sends two to three humans.
{{QUEST_CREWDEAD_START}} is a job to take a ship **intact**. Destroy the target instead and the wreck costs you 13 hull, a random system, and one room hit with every effect at once.

{{ROCK_STARSHIP_MINE}} chews through the hull while you decide: a missile detonation costs 3 hull, a beam drone costs a drone part, and defusing it by hand can drop into a red-wire/blue-wire flip where the wrong end kills the volunteer, takes 5 hull and opens a breach. Engines 5 backs you out of the whole thing for nothing.

Rock is the exception to the note above: the distress line is filled **before** the neutral pool, not after, so the extra marker that {{ASTEROID_DERELICT_SHIP}} carries comes from the very bottom of the table and is the first one a full map loses. Two events in the distress line show no marker at all, so an ordinary-looking beacon can still be one of them.

Long-Ranged Scanners split the marked beacons exactly one way here: a possible-ship reading means {{FRIENDLY_BEACON}}, {{ESCORT_BEACON}} or {{TRAP_BEACON}} — two payouts and one ambush. Every other distress beacon in the sector reports as a plain unvisited location.

Two, fixed, no roll, and first in the fill order — the shopping is the one guarantee this sector makes. Anything beyond it is an event opening a shop, and two of the three that can are in the 0–1 quest line.

The sector allocates no nebula line, so no purple clouds are drawn on the map: sensors work at every beacon, no jump you make slows the pursuit, and every hazard here is a sun or an asteroid field you can see coming with scanners.
